insurer: ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Limited

good.name: PED Waiting
good.quote: Pre-existing diseases: Covered after 24 months (48 months, for plans with Sum Insured up to 2Lacs) of continuous coverage.
good.reference: Key Information Sheet, S.No 6(a); Policy Wording Part II, Clause 3.1
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are covered after 24 months for most plans, or 48 months if the sum insured is up to ₹2 lakhs. This means you must keep the policy active for 2 years before claiming for pre-existing conditions.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage
good.explanation: Treatment for specified illnesses is excluded for the first 24 months of coverage. You need to wait 2 years before claiming for these specific conditions.

good.name: Initial Waiting
good.quote: Initial waiting period: 30 days for all illnesses (except Hospitalisation due to injury).
good.reference: Key Information Sheet, S.No 6(d); Policy Wording Part II, Clause 3.4
good.explanation: Illnesses are covered only after a 30-day waiting period, while hospitalizations due to injury are covered immediately. This means you cannot claim for illnesses occurring within the first month of policy start.

good.name: Restore Benefit
good.quote: For plans with Sum Insured ` 3lacs and above, We will reset up to 100% of the Sum insured once in a policy year... The reset amount can only be used for all future claims within the same policy year, not related to the illness/ disease/ injury for which a claim has been paid in that policy year for the same person
good.reference: Policy Wording Part II, Section 2 (Scope of Cover), E) Reset Benefit
good.explanation: Sum insured is replenished once per policy year for unrelated illnesses if your sum insured is ₹3 lakhs or more. This helps cover new illnesses but not repeated claims for the same condition in the same year.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization
good.quote: Pre-hospitalisation Medical Expenses incurred by You for a 30-day period immediately prior to Your Hospitalisation
good.explanation: Medical expenses up to 30 days before hospitalization are covered. This helps you claim costs related to diagnosis and treatment leading to hospital admission.

good.name: Post-hospitalization
good.quote: Post-hospitalisation Medical Expenses incurred by You for a 60-day period immediately post Hospitalisation
good.explanation: Medical expenses up to 60 days after discharge are covered. This supports recovery costs following hospitalization.

bad.name: Room Rent
bad.quote: Room Rent means the amount charged by a hospital for the occupancy of a bed on per day (24 hours) basis and shall include associated medical expenses.
bad.reference: Policy Wording Part II, Definitions (Room Rent)
bad.explanation: The policy does not specify any room rent limit or room category, implying possible caps or restrictions elsewhere. Lack of clarity on room rent can lead to proportionate deductions and higher out-of-pocket costs.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: Below are the non payable items applicable in the policy... GLOVES... SYRINGES / PPE-type items etc. (listed as non payable items)
bad.reference: Policy document section: "Non Payables" / "List of Non Payable Items as per IRDAI"
bad.explanation: Many common hospital consumables like gloves and syringes are excluded from coverage. This means you may have to pay these costs yourself during hospitalization.

bad.name: Cashless Network
bad.quote: Cashless Facility available at over 4000+ network hospitals.
bad.explanation: The cashless hospital network includes just over 4,000 hospitals, which is below the market standard of 7,000+. This may limit your convenience and choice for cashless treatment.

bad.name: Disease Sub-limits
bad.quote: Cataract, where sub-limit of ` 20,000/- is applicable per eye per Policy year for Plans with Sum Insured up to 5 Lacs. Sub limit of ` 1,00,000 per eye per Policy year will be applicable for cataract treatment for plans with Sum Insured above ` 5Lacs
bad.reference: Key Information Sheet, S.No 8(a); Policy Wording Part II, Clause 3.2 (Cataract*)
bad.explanation: Cataract treatment has fixed monetary caps per eye, which can restrict claim amounts especially for lower sum insured plans. This limits coverage for this common procedure.

bad.name: Disease Sub-limits
bad.quote: Extension 15: Sub Limits on Medical Expenses/ Illness/ Surgeries/ Procedures... Our maximum liability... shall be limited as per the table below
bad.explanation: If selected, this extension imposes multiple procedure-wise caps on claims, restricting payouts for common surgeries. This can significantly reduce your claim amount if these sub-limits apply.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: Co-payment means a cost sharing requirement under a health insurance policy that provides that the policyholder/ insured/ proposer will bear a specified percentage of the admissible claims amount.
bad.explanation: The policy defines co-payment but does not specify if or when it applies or the percentage involved. You need to check the policy schedule to understand if any co-pay is applicable.

unclear.name: NCB
unclear.quote: An Additional Sum Insured of 10% of Annual Sum Insured provided on each renewal for every claim-free year up to a maximum of 50%. In case of a claim under the policy, the accumulated Additional Sum Insured will be reduced by 10% of the Annual Sum Insured in the following year.
unclear.reference: Key Information Sheet, S.No 10(a); Policy Wording Part II, Section 2(G) Additional Sum Insured (Cumulative Bonus)
unclear.explanation: No claim bonus increases sum insured by 10% per claim-free year but reduces by 10% after a claim. The exact reset behavior and minimum floor are not clearly stated, so confirm details from the policy schedule.

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
